It's right opposite Antilia, so it's pretty easy to locate with a few parking spots as well.

I recently visited with my cat for her vaccination and overall check-up, and as always, Dr. Vineet handled her with such care. Despite her being very scared, he performed a thorough check-up gently and patiently, and also guided us with our newly adopted indie pup. What I truly value is how his strong medical expertise is complemented by his deep understanding of animal behaviour and psychology, which makes his advice both practical for us and stress-free for the pets.

South Mumbai finally has a one-of-a-kind clinic, and I couldn’t be more grateful! Despite so many clinics being there, we finally have one which doesn't make you wait during emergencies and their treatment can be trusted!

Advice: Call in advance and take an appointment to avoid waiting too long for your turn.

featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Mr. Salvi, we are surprised to see this review as you haven't visited our premises yourself and it was Ms. Padawe who brought Pintu in. We are unaware of how you are connected to this case but we would still like to clarify.

We are sorry that you feel this way and would like to bring you some relief by actually narrating what really happened at our premises. Pintu was presented with inappetence and weakness, and all diagnostics, treatment plans, and estimated costs were discussed, signed and approved before proceeding by Ms. Padawe. Throughout her diagnostic tests and treatment, we provided updates regarding her condition as she was boarded with us for medical supervision through the day.

The statement that an additional ₹7,000 was suddenly demanded before leaving is completely inaccurate. The amount was discussed and approved beforehand and was for a specific diagnostic test that was strongly suggested because we needed to arrive at a definitive diagnosis with no prior history of an indoor-outdoor cat like Pintu. 

It is also important to understand that cats suffering from infectious or systemic illnesses may not recover completely within a single day of treatment. Improvement often requires several days of consistent medication, supportive care, and follow-up monitoring.

Regarding the concern that Pintu ran away after receiving her medication, there is no medical basis to conclude that the prescribed medication caused her to leave the house, as you mentioned that she is an indoor outdoor cat already. Cats experiencing illness, stress, or discomfort may hide or become less visible, and this behavior was part of the original concerns for which she was presented, infact you mentioned  she was so weak that she couldn't move and after treatment she had enough energy to run away from home when tried to feed medication. At the time, we provided guidance and continued to assist you through messages regarding her care at home multiple times.

We also provided advice regarding medication administration and feeding, and recommended that Pintu be brought back for treatment if you don't see an improvement in her condition after she returned home. Unfortunately, the recommended follow-up treatment was not carried out by you.

We fully understand how distressing it is when a pet is unwell. However, it is important that the outcome of a medical case be assessed based on the complete course of treatment and follow-up rather than just the first 12 hours after discharge.

Our team remains committed to providing transparent communication, appropriate medical care, and support to every patient and pet owner.  

After leaving us the above review Ms. Padawe still reached out to ask for more assistance and we still happily obliged as it's Pintu's wellbeing that has always been our priority. 
We sincerely wish Pintu a full and speedy recovery and honestly hope that you follow through with the recommended diagnostics and treatment wherever you choose to take Pintu

featured_reviews.name: Mamta Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I hate this clinic. I recommend you all not to visit this clinic at all. They only know to kill animals and earn money by giving them various medicines. I lost my 50 days puppy on 12 July. I visited the clinic yesterday at 7.30 pm and she was suffering from diaherrea since last 5 days and she wasn't vomiting at all. We gave her some medicines orally which was fine and made her improved. That day she only did once the diarrhea and we thought to visit the clinic that evening to cure her as soon as possible and unfortunately we visited the worst place ever.

First they did her parvovirus test which was ok we thought that it would be some kind of formalities to check whether she is fine or not but then her report was negative . After that they took her inside the cabin and everything was just secretly done inside the cabin. All could I was able to hear her loud whining and crying voice from inside. They don't allow pet owners to be present with their pets inside the cabin. The dr name Manali asked us to check for blood test and she told to have the IV(injection) the medicines which we were giving her orally and I don't even know what kind of IV they gave that after coming out of the cabin she was totally collapsing and fainting at home. They told us to admit her and they only talked us about the amount and charges. We didn't agreed to admit her b'coz we leave near by so after coming outside the cabin she started vomiting continuously and she was not even able to stand and walk. They did not told us prior that after giving IV she would also die and will also start vomiting. My puppy was totally fine but they made her too weak that she also had blood loss in her diaherrea and unfortunately today morning she left her soul.
Crown Vet Clinic is the most greedy clinic and only wants to earn instead of saving animals. After the checkup and IV they increased the amount of the bill.
Today I called at the clinic to know the reason that what was in the IV that she died and the dr Manali wasn't accepting her mistake that she gave her over dose. Dr Manali injected the medicines on her neck and due to which maybe the medicine affected on her brain. The pet owners are waiting outside the cabin hoping about their loved ones, their pets would cure and become healthy but they aren't trust worthy at all
Today it happened and affected our family and I don't want this to be happen in another family. If you want to visit then pls take at your own risk if you truly love your pets and also go inside the cabin with the doctors to have a look what they do with your pets.

From my personal experience I would suggest not to visit this clinic at any cost.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Ms Mamta,
We are truly sorry for the loss of your puppy and understand the pain of losing a beloved companion.
Based on our internal investigation, we would like to respond to your concerns as follows.
We strongly object to the inaccurate and offensive language used in your review, especially given the circumstances under which your pet was brought to us and we ensured proper treatment was provided.
Your puppy was presented at our Worli clinic on the evening of 12th July in a critical condition, with a history of 5 days of diarrhea and visible dehydration, pale mucous membranes, and weakness post visiting another clinic for the same concern. Our veterinarian, Dr. Manali immediately conducted a thorough examination, including a Parvo test (which was negative) and blood tests, all with your consent and ensured immediate treatment was started.
Based on clinical signs and diagnostics, hospitalization with aggressive fluid therapy was strongly advised and the charges were well explained. However, you declined hospitalization, citing that you lived nearby and preferred to monitor her at home and also mentioned cost constraints. This decision was made despite being clearly informed that the puppy’s condition was serious and could deteriorate rapidly without hospitalization.
The decision to discharge the pet and proceed with home care was made contrary to the attending veterinarian’s professional recommendation. In light of this, it became necessary to first stabilize the pet’s condition to the extent possible to facilitate a safe transition. Intravenous fluids and medications were administered, as they offer a more immediate and effective response in acute cases compared to oral medications, which had been used previously. These interventions were carried out in full accordance with established veterinary protocols. The intravenous access was secured via the jugular vein—a standard and clinically appropriate route—due to its size and reliability in such medical scenarios.
While we understand your concerns about not being present during the procedure, please note that for safety, sterility, and minimal stress to the pet, it is standard veterinary practice to perform medical procedures in a controlled space without pet parents present.
The assumption that the medication provided in the IV was the reason for the pet's death is unfounded and totally inaccurate.
Also as you stated “Dr Manali injected the medicines on her neck and due to which maybe the medicine affected her brain”, this is completely baseless and an assumption made by you. We assure you injecting medication in the neck is a common practice and does not affect the brain as you assume it to.
In spite of us informing you about the critical condition of your pet, you chose to take her home instead of admitting her. In this case it seems unfair to shift the blame on our clinic. We would also like to assure you no overdosage or inappropriate medication was given, and at every stage, our team communicated transparently and professionally.
Crown Vet has been serving the veterinary community for over 10 years, with a team of qualified and experienced doctors who prioritize animal care above all else. We do not accept the defamatory statements made against our staff and clinic, and we stand firmly by the care provided in this case.
While we deeply empathize with your loss, we would also like to highlight that your review does not paint a clear picture of how our Vets did their best to persuade you to admit the pet for her benefit.
Regards,
Crown Vet.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr. Akshay 😇 I can’t find words to describe this man! Such words have not yet been invented in any language! My story is 7 months long.
On April 6, one of my children all got sick at once, 6 puppies near my house. I urgently flew from Mumbai home to Varanasi, what I saw tore my heart into small pieces! They were paralyzed! I realized that this was a nervous plague. But I have never encountered this before, I don’t know how to treat it, and the most annoying thing is that we don’t have doctors in Varanasi who would be so professional. It was hell. Between changing diapers and calming the children, in tears, I read veterinary forums and literature. I called hundreds of veterinarians in Russia. And most of them recommended euthanization. I just can’t explain to the Russian people that according to our religion, we cannot take anyone’s life. I tried... I tried everything! Everything I could! We even got the serum delivered from Mumbai. I went to a human medical school, but out of desperation, I learned how to give IVs to dogs. Nobody wants to help me, everyone shrugged their shoulders, but I was simply dying from pain and hopelessness. I prayed day and night for Shiva and Ganesha to decide and either take them away or for them to go to recovery. Day after day, week after week, month after month. I did massages and continued to fight the plague. The children died in my arms, and by lowering them into the Ganges, I also lowered part of my heart. Of all the people, only Snezhana was able to defeat the plague! But she also remained bedridden. Bedsores, heart and kidney failure, then diarrhea and constipation began. The only thing that remained unchanged was his excellent appetite.How many tears I shed is known only to the gods. And the day came when my visa expired.... I took Snezhana to animal Rescue....
And I thought that I would never see her again. In Rescue, no one had time for massages and her bedsores became bone-chip. I was dying sitting in Russia, on my knees at the consulate so that they would quickly check my documents. But they kept dragging on (they were embarrassed by my appearance, although I offered to put me on a polygraph and they were convinced that I had never used anything), at that moment they found a tumor on my dad, and it just pulled me to the window, just to jump and not suffer anymore. But I continued to pray and Ganesha brought me a Russian guy who agreed to watch Snezhana and do a massage. I rented them a room in the house where Snezhana was born (my room is also there). But he didn’t have enough energy for a massage. Her paws became like those of a female praying mantis. I watched the video every day and lost hope.... Until Ganesh Chaturthi came! A Pandit from India came to Moscow, I went to pray, we got into a conversation and he asked, “During the yagya, was it uncomfortable for you to sit?”, I told him my story of a spinal fracture and how I stood up thanks to Ganesha and also mentioned that acupuncture helped me a lot!
The text continues in the photo, the whole story didn't fit.
